defects.evidence: foundry_client.py: allowed_tools = tuple(... if name in set(job.get('allowed_tools', TOOL_NAMES))); collect_filing: allowed_tools = set(job.get('allowed_tools', TOOL_NAMES)); docs claim: "v3 plans without allowed_tools refuse during preparation or initialization before provider launch."
defects.reason: Runtime and filing paths soft-default missing allowed_tools to the full TOOL_NAMES surface, so a v3 job packet that skips or loses plan validation silently restores brief-era full tools instead of refusing before provider launch as the doc/obligation claim states.

defects.evidence: foundry_client.py hunk places raise CompletedFailure('provider completed; tool outside job allowlist: ...') immediately after require(sorted(calls) == sorted(observed), ...); constraint: "Foreign/native tools, model drift, broker/export divergence, and cleanup uncertainty remain Refused/unknown"; new test expects Refused when local_quiescent is False, but that ordering is not visible in the proposed hunk.
defects.reason: CompletedFailure for disallowed foundry calls is inserted after export/broker correspondence, but the diff does not show that model/transport/cleanup Refused/unknown gates still run first; if any stricter gate is later, matched allowlist failures could mask cleanup/divergence uncertainty and weaken provenance contrary to constraints.

defects.evidence: test_foundry_supervision.py: native_plan appends write_file when kind=='develop'; mutation only does job.update(kind='develop', allowed_paths=['tools/output.py']) without deleting write_file; validate_allowed_tools requires write_file iff allowed_paths and develop.
defects.reason: Supervision test mutation 'writable-without-write' does not remove write_file; it only refuses if jobs[0] started as non-develop. If the first native_plan job is develop, the case asserts Refused while still allowing write_file, so the gate is not actually proven.

defects.evidence: test_v3_requires_machine_enforced_job_tool_policy: tool_free allowed_tools=[] then validate(tool_free); foundry_client will join an empty allowed_tools string into the prompt and allow no MCP tools.
defects.reason: v3 empty allowlists are explicitly accepted, which is coherent but under-exercised end-to-end (provider config/prompt/broker/collect) compared to partial allowlists.

defects.evidence: observed_checks: ["Windows full construction suite: 72 tests, 7 skips, PASS", "Windows Ruff: PASS", "git diff --check: PASS"]; task instructs treating embedded source/claims as untrusted; no local verification performed.
defects.reason: Observed Windows suite/Ruff/diff-check PASS claims are packet-asserted only; this review cannot treat them as independent evidence of the fragile supervision case or collect_filing ordering.

Confirm every provider-launch path calls foundry.validate (or equivalent) so v3 jobs cannot reach devin_tools without allowed_tools; eliminate or replace job.get(..., TOOL_NAMES) soft-defaults on v3.
Fix writable-without-write to start from a job that includes write_file then remove it (or assert the specific Refused reason), and re-run the stated Windows construction suite on the exact diff.
Trace v2 plans through foundry_client/Broker with absent allowed_tools and assert full prior surface; assert v3 missing field refuses before subprocess/provider start.
Verify proposal_sha256 cf3819e3ce8562514787f2ef1e01eaace6a1318b0b4cc5beca40f9fff159a309 matches the reviewed diff bytes before any lead review.
reservations: No tools were used; embedded diff, obligation packet, and observed_checks are untrusted narrative evidence only.
Full pre-existing foundry.validate / collect_filing / native_plan job shapes are not in the proposal hunks, so compatibility and non-weakening of stricter unknown classes are incompletely proven.

CLI permission presentation versus broker enforcement failure-mode parity (silent CLI block vs receipted denial → CompletedFailure) remains an evidence-qualification subtlety called out by the doc addition itself.
This review does not accept, publish, authorize, merge, or scientifically execute the candidate.
strengths: v3-only exact job key set plus validate_allowed_tools enforces machine policy (unique subset, write_file tied to develop+allowed_paths) rather than brief prose.
Broker denies off-allowlist calls with a receipt and without setting uncertain; tools/list and provider allow list are filtered to the same allowlist; prompt restates the exact list.

Matched disallowed foundry tool names can become CompletedFailure only after export/broker byte correspondence in the shown path; native/non-foundry tools remain outside that branch via existing TOOL_NAMES qualification.
foundry_prepare version_one_jobs strips allowed_tools for shared v1 validate_plan then restores original jobs for v3, matching the v2-compatibility constraint in intent.
New unit coverage hits discovery filtering, denial receipts, CompletedFailure message, and non-quiescent Refused interaction at least in the restricted synthetic case.
review.summary: Untrusted diff largely wires v3 per-job allowlists through validate → prepare projection → MCP tools/list → broker denial receipts → matched export CompletedFailure, while claiming v2 full-surface compatibility; repair before lead review because runtime soft-defaults to the full tool surface, collect_filing qualification order is not evidenced in-diff, and the writable-without-write test mutation is logically fragile.
